subject: Next steps: Procurement readiness & commercial path for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme.com>, Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + procurement questions

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Key notes from the call:
- Use case: Acme wants to add LLM-powered assistance to your internal support portal (document retrieval + summarization).
- Expected traffic: POC ~5k monthly requests, production could ramp to ~1M tokens/day in 6-9 months.
- Security: data-in-transit encryption required; SOC 2 + audit logs are gating for production.

Procurement/commercial items we discussed:
1) Procurement readiness: do you require a PO for pilot/POC or is card acceptable for initial pilot?
2) Paper process: estimated internal review timeline, any specific legal requirements (customer-specific terms)?
3) Marketplace: interest in purchasing via cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/Google)?

Attachments: Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (checklist for procurement team)

Recommended next steps:
- Jordan/Sofia: confirm whether card is OK for pilot and whether production will require PO + Net terms.
- Marissa (me) / Aditya: we’ll send an initial SOW + 2 pricing paths (pilot hosted on our API vs dedicated reserved capacity) and a short set of contract highlights.
- If marketplace is preferred, let us know which provider and we’ll surface listing options and timing.

I’ll follow up with the SOW and pricing doc later today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, procurement-team@acme.com, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Quick answers from our side:

1) Pilot/PO: For a small POC (<$5k) we can use a company card. Production deployments will require a PO and Net30 payment terms; finance will push for a PO.
2) Paper/legal: We typically require our standard master services agreement (MSA) with a few redlines around liability and data handling. Legal review usually takes 7-10 business days once we have draft docs.
3) Marketplace: We're interested in AWS Marketplace but will need to confirm internal procurement routing — if listing helps, it's a plus.

I'll attach the procurement intake form so you can see what our finance team needs. We'll aim to route the PO request the week of June 7th if the SOW & pricing look good.

Attachments: Acme_Procurement_Form.pdf

—Jordan
Jordan Matthews
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme.com>, Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions

Thanks Jordan — this is perfect. Quick follow-up to make procurement routing simpler and to show recommended commercial paths based on your usage profile:

Options we recommend:
A) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest time to value, card-friendly for pilots, on-demand billing. For production, we support PO + Net terms. Good for teams that want minimal ops and fast integration.
B) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — dedicated GPU pools; recommended when you expect sustained high throughput. Requires commited monthly/annual commit for pricing discounts; procurement will want a reservation addendum on the contract.
C) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — for regulated workloads that need customer-managed networking and stricter controls. Longer procurement and deployment timeline; usually enterprise licensing + support fee.

Commercial considerations for Acme:
- Pilot: Hosted API on card to start (keeps procurement out of the critical path).
- Production: Looks like you’ll want PO + Net30; if production token volume > X we should evaluate a Reserved/Dedicated commit to reduce unit costs.
- Marketplace: Listing on AWS Marketplace can simplify PO routing for some customers; we can provide a marketplace quote in parallel.

I’ve attached the pricing options and a draft SOW that maps to the pilot scope we discussed. Please review and let me know which path you prefer so we can surface the right contract and procurement artifacts.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Options.pdf; Draft_SOW_Acme.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions

Looping in a couple of notes from pricing/ops that may help with procurement conversations:

- Commit guidance: For teams hitting >500k tokens/day sustained, Dedicated with a 12-month commit typically gives the best unit economics. We can show tiered commit options (3mo pilot commit, 6mo, 12mo) with blended discounts.
- On-demand vs commit: On-demand (hosted) keeps you flexible but is higher per-token. We can offer a short-term pilot discount if you sign up for a 3-month commit window.
- Marketplace vs PO: AWS Marketplace purchases can be done via PO but sometimes have additional fees and slower payouts. If finance prefers a single PO and consolidated billing, we’ll provide an AWS Marketplace listing quote and SOW to match.

If you want, we can prepare two commercial packages today:
1) Pilot package: Hosted API, card OK, limit = 5k requests/month, SOW + invoice with card option.
2) Production package: PO + Net30, option A = Hosted with higher volume pricing; option B = Dedicated with commit tiers and reserved pricing.

I’ve attached a sample contract addendum that covers reserved capacity and marketplace purchases — feel free to share with your legal/procurement folks.

Attachments: Sample_Reserved_Addendum.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
